usageNotes: Lists all CIDR entries inside a named IPSet scoped to a specific VM's firewall. The IPSet must already exist on that VM — use the list-ipsets endpoint first if the name is unknown. Each returned entry includes the CIDR, an optional comment, a digest (use it as an optimistic-lock token for subsequent writes), and an optional 'nomatch' flag that inverts the entry's match behavior.

examples.summary: List all entries in the 'trusted-mgmt' IPSet for VM 110 on node pve1

tips: The 'digest' field in each entry is used to prevent concurrent modifications — pass it when updating or deleting an entry to ensure the set hasn't changed since you read it.
The 'nomatch' flag negates a CIDR entry, effectively creating an exclusion within the IPSet — useful for carving out a subnet from a broader range.
IPSet names must start with a letter and can only contain letters, digits, hyphens, and underscores (2–64 chars).
This endpoint is VM-firewall scoped; cluster-level IPSets live under a different path (/cluster/firewall/ipset/{name}).
